clinician.final_diagnosis: Ewing's sarcoma with metastatic pulmonary and bone marrow dissemination
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old boy presented with a 3-week progressive illness characterized by initial 3-day fever followed by persistent asthenia and progressive cough. He also developed a thoracic urticarial rash and lower back pain. On admission, he had fever (38°C) and mildly impaired general condition but no hemodynamic or respiratory instability. Laboratory findings revealed elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 5.71 mg/dL, IL-6 70.9 pg/mL, ferritin 668 ng/mL), markedly elevated LDH (2.517 U/L) indicating high tumor burden, elevated D-dimer (5.161 µg/mL), mild coagulopathy (INR 1.3), and mild anemia (hemoglobin 133 g/dL). Chest X-ray showed bilateral interstitial infiltrates. High-resolution CT of the thorax revealed diffuse pulmonary nodules with mediastinal widening and lytic bone lesions affecting the dorsal vertebrae, sternum, and second right costal arch. Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated small round blue cells suggestive of solid tumor infiltration. Bone biopsy and SPECT imaging were performed. Once the presumptive diagnosis of an oncological process was established, COVID-19 treatment was discontinued, hyperhydration and rasburicase were initiated, and the patient was transferred to a pediatric oncohaematology reference center for definitive diagnosis and treatment.
